title: X-ray Spectral Softening in AO 0235+164: Swift-XRT Analysis and Class-S Classification (C3 Complete Sample Final)
abstract: Systematic Swift-XRT hardness ratio analysis of AO 0235+164 (ISP BL Lac, z=0.94) using 180 observations (63,028 photons) spanning 2007–2024. Result: β=−0.682, r=−0.434, p=1.14×10⁻⁹ → Class-S (spectral softening). This completes the C3 Complete Sample Classification: 11 ISP BL Lac objects from 4LAC-DR3 high, H:1 (TXS 0506+056, neutrino-confirmed) / S:10, total 277,743 photons. Probability by chance ≈0.6%. Predicts future neutrino-emitting blazars will exhibit Class-H (spectral hardening) behavior. Related: DOI:10.5281/zenodo.19803698 (ISP v7), DOI:10.5281/zenodo.19807060 (C3 Complete).
keywords: blazar, ISP BL Lac, Swift-XRT, AO 0235+164, neutrino, IceCube, spectral variability, Class-S, 4LAC, X-ray spectroscopy

title: Complete X-Ray Spectral Classification of ISP Blazars in the 4LAC-DR3 High-Variability Sample: A Ten-Source Swift-XRT Hardness Ratio Study and the Class-S/H Neutrino Prediction Framework
abstract: We present the complete X-ray spectral classification of all 10 ISP BL Lac objects in the 4LAC-DR3 high-variability blazar sample using Swift-XRT hardness ratio analysis. Total: 214,715 photons across ~191 observations (2005–2023). Result: 9/10 sources are Class-S (spectral softening, leptonic), 1/10 (TXS 0506+056) is Class-H (spectral hardening, hadronic) — the only confirmed astrophysical neutrino blazar. New classifications: MG1 J021114+1051 (Class-S, β=−1.144, p=8.15e-4), PMN J0531-4827 (Class-S, β=−5.069, p=2.41e-4), TXS 1055+567 (Class-S tentative, p=0.101). IceCube candidates PKS 0735+178 (IC-211208A) and PKS B1424-418 (HESE-35) are both Class-S, disfavoring neutrino production. The Class-S/H framework is now established on a complete, well-defined sample as a falsifiable predictive tool for multimessenger blazar astronomy. Probability of this H:1/S:9 result by chance: ~0.1%.
keywords: blazar, ISP, Swift-XRT, hardness ratio, neutrino, IceCube, Class-S, Class-H, multimessenger astronomy, 4LAC-DR3, TXS 0506+056, complete sample, spectral classification

title: Complete Class-S/H Classification of the C3 ISP Blazar Sample: All 10 Sources via Swift-XRT Hardness Ratio Analysis
abstract: We present the complete X-ray spectral classification of all 10 ISP BL Lac objects in the 4LAC-DR3 high-variability sample using Swift-XRT hardness ratio (HR) analysis. The C3 (Complete Classification of C3) sample comprises: TXS 0506+056 (Class-H, confirmed neutrino source), and 9 Class-S sources (W Comae, S5 0716+714, 3C 66A, ON 246, PKS 0735+178, PKS B1424-418, MG1 J021114+1051, PMN J0531-4827, TXS 1055+567). Total sample: 214,715 photons across all observations. The sole Class-H source (TXS 0506+056) is the only confirmed astrophysical neutrino blazar. All 9 Class-S sources show negative HR vs. count-rate slopes, consistent with leptonic X-ray emission. This complete sample firmly establishes the Class-S/H framework as a predictive tool for identifying neutrino-emitting blazars: Class-H = hadronic/neutrino candidate; Class-S = leptonic, neutrino production disfavored. New analyses: MG1 J021114+1051 (β=−1.144, p=8.15e-4, 24 obs, N=13,254), PMN J0531-4827 (β=−5.069, p=2.41e-4, 6 obs,
keywords: blazar, ISP, Swift-XRT, hardness ratio, neutrino, IceCube, Class-S, Class-H, multimessenger, 4LAC-DR3, complete sample

title: X-Ray Spectral Softening in the IceCube HESE-35 Candidate Blazar PKS B1424-418: A Class-S Classification via Swift-XRT Hardness Ratio Analysis
abstract: We present a systematic Swift-XRT hardness ratio (HR) analysis of PKS B1424-418 (z=0.452), proposed as a counterpart to IceCube HESE-35 ('Big Bird', ~2013 April, PeV-scale neutrino). Using 73 archival PC-mode observations spanning 2005–2023 (total N=95,313 photons), we find β=−0.696 (r=−0.762, p=4.87×10⁻¹⁵) in HR vs. count rate — firmly Class-S (spectral softening). The 2014 intensive monitoring campaign (29 observations) shows consistent softening during and after the HESE-35 epoch. A 2023-05-25 extreme flare (HR=−0.674, CR=1.348 cts/s) is the most extreme leptonic state recorded. Within the Class-S/H framework (Katayama 2026a/b), PKS B1424-418 is predicted not to be the primary neutrino source of HESE-35. The sole confirmed neutrino blazar TXS 0506+056 is Class-H. This is the most statistically significant Class-S classification in our 7-source sample (p=4.87×10⁻¹⁵, ~15σ).
keywords: blazar, PKS B1424-418, IceCube HESE-35, Big Bird, Swift-XRT, hardness ratio, neutrino, multimessenger astronomy, Class-S, spectral classification, X-ray astronomy

title: X-Ray Spectral Softening in the IceCube-211208A Candidate Blazar PKS 0735+178: A Class-S Classification via Swift-XRT Hardness Ratio Analysis
abstract: Systematic Swift-XRT hardness ratio analysis of PKS 0735+178 (z=0.424), a proposed counterpart to IceCube-211208A (separation 2.2°). Using 24 archival PC-mode observations spanning 2009–2022 (N=14,917 photons), we find β=−0.706 (r=−0.579, p=3.0×10⁻³) in HR vs. count rate, classifying PKS 0735+178 as Class-S (spectral softening at high flux). During the December 2021 IceCube campaign, the source showed its softest spectra at high flux — inconsistent with hadronic neutrino production. The confirmed neutrino blazar TXS 0506+056 is Class-H (β>0). Within the Class-S/H framework (Katayama 2026, DOI:10.5281/zenodo.19803698), PKS 0735+178 is predicted not to be the primary neutrino source of IceCube-211208A.
keywords: blazar, PKS 0735+178, IceCube-211208A, Swift-XRT, hardness ratio, neutrino, multimessenger, Class-S, BL Lac

title: Quasi-Periodic Oscillations in C3 ISP Blazars: Evidence from Fermi-LAT FAVA 17-Year Light Curves
abstract: We present a Lomb-Scargle periodicity analysis of five Intermediate-frequency Peaked BL Lac objects (ISP blazars) belonging to the C3 clustering group, using 17 years (2008–2025) of weekly Fermi-LAT FAVA σ-excess light curves. All five sources exhibit statistically significant quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) with false alarm probabilities ranging from 5.8×10⁻⁴ to 1.3×10⁻²⁶. The dominant periods span 2.2–7.7 years, consistent with binary supermassive black hole precession or jet helical structure. The Class-H source TXS 0506+056—the only confirmed neutrino-emitting blazar—shows a QPO period of 3.92 years, with the IceCube-170922A event falling on the rising limb of a predicted high-state. ON 246 exhibits the strongest periodicity (FAP=1.3×10⁻²⁶, T=4.10 yr). These results strengthen the C3/Class-H classification framework and provide falsifiable predictions for future neutrino-coincident flare windows from TXS 0506+056.
keywords: blazars, BL Lac objects, quasi-periodic oscillations, Fermi-LAT, FAVA, neutrino emission, hadronic jets, TXS 0506+056, lomb-scargle, C3 ISP blazars, ON 246

title: Detection-Limit Hypothesis: N_min ∝ Fvar² — Empirical Verification Across Five C3 ISP Blazars
abstract: We present empirical verification of the Detection-Limit Hypothesis using Swift XRT archival data from five C3 ISP blazars (ON 246, 3C 66A, TXS 0506+056, W Comae, S5 0716+714). The hypothesis states that the minimum photon count N_min required to statistically detect a given spectral change |ΔHR| scales as N_min ∝ Fvar², where Fvar is the fractional variability amplitude. Log-log regression across five independent sources yields an empirical slope of 2.016 (theoretical prediction: 2.0), with r=0.652. The W Comae / S5 0716+714 pair provides the cleanest test: both sources share Fvar ≈ 0.87, yet S5 0716+714 (N=33,064) achieves KS p<0.001 while W Comae (N=5,956) remains at p=0.072 — detection-limited by photon count alone. This relationship predicts W Comae spectral softening will be confirmed at p<0.05 with approximately 30,000 photons, testable with a single deep Swift XRT observation. title: Statistical Substructure of ISP Blazar Variability: Five-Source Analysis and Class-S/Class-H Spectral Bifurcation
abstract: Five-source Swift XRT analysis of C3 ISP blazars. TXS 0506+056 (15,690 photons) and S5 0716+714 (33,064 photons) added to the three-source v6 sample. Reveals spectral bifurcation: Class-S (softening, 4/5 sources, leptonic) vs Class-H (hardening, TXS 0506+056, hadronic candidate). TXS 0506+056 shows ΔHR = +0.199, p = 0.0029, KS p = 0.0015. Detection-Limit Hypothesis quantified as N_min ∝ Fvar². Predicts neutrino-emitting blazars preferentially exhibit Class-H X-ray spectral behavior.
keywords: blazars, ISP, Swift XRT, TXS 0506+056, S5 0716+714, IceCube, neutrino, Class-H, hadronic, 4LAC-DR3

title: ON 246 and the Stochastic Self-Organized Criticality in C3 ISP Blazars: A Weekly Light Curve Analysis
abstract: Weekly-cadence Fermi-LAT light curve analysis of the C3 ISP blazar subpopulation identified in Katayama (2026a, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19776343). We identify two temporally distinct variability archetypes: SOC-type (burst/dormant, ON 246: max/min=72.6x, skewness=3.57, ACF significant at lags 1-10 weeks) and continuous-type (sustained oscillation, S5 0716+71: near-Gaussian distribution). The 'clogged turbine vs. running engine' dichotomy suggests physically distinct jet internal states coexisting within the ISP transition zone. C3 is not one thing — within the anomalous, it is heterogeneous.

title: Statistical Evidence for Multi-Population Structure in ISP Blazars: Limitations of SED-Based Classification
abstract:
Preprint version. Not yet peer-reviewed.

We investigate the luminosity distribution of ISP blazars in the Fermi-LAT 4LAC-DR3 catalog (N=246). After accounting for redshift-dependent effects via luminosity-bin normalization, the ISP luminosity distribution exhibits statistically significant non-Gaussianity (skewness=-0.908, Anderson-Darling p<0.001) that persists after accounting for several commonly used physical proxies (variability index, nu_syn, PL_Index), and remains after both linear and non-linear regression approaches (including Random Forest). GMM decomposition (k=3, selected via BIC minimization) identifies three statistically distinct sub-populations with significant differences in beaming and luminosity (Kruskal-Wallis p<0.001), but no difference in nu_syn (p=0.961) — the defining parameter of ISP classification. title: ΔP_間 Hypothesis: Observational Evidence and Open Questions for the Next Generation — A Beaming-Controlled Residual Analysis of AGN Jet Luminosity Distributions
abstract: Beaming-proxy-controlled residual analysis of AGN jet luminosity distributions using NASA Fermi LAT 4LAC-DR3 (1,532 sources). Primary finding: LSP-class blazars show beaming-dominant distributions with negative skewness (−0.91), contradicting the original upward-excess prediction of ΔP_間. ISP-class blazars show statistically significant non-normality (AD=1.20 > critical 0.75) after beaming control (KS_p=0.142), while HSP shows no anomaly. The ISP result is presented as a precisely defined open question — not as evidence for ΔP_間 — with four candidate explanations (observation bias, uncontrolled physical quantities, classification boundary artifact, mixture distribution) that must be eliminated before ΔP_間 can be considered. This paper marks today's natural boundary and passes the question forward to the next generation. Full process record (including overstatement, correction, rejected post-hoc modification): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19715157.
keywords: AGN jets, blazars, Fermi LAT, 4LAC-DR3, ΔP_間, Genki Universe, dual-universe hypothesis, beaming correction, residual analysis, ISP blazars, open questions, falsifiability, Katayama hypothesis

title: [CORRECTED] Observational Evidence for ΔP_間: Statistical Excess in AGN Jet Energy Output — Preliminary Exploration Only
abstract: CORRECTION ISSUED SAME DAY (April 24, 2026). The original paper overstated its findings. The analysis conducted was a KS normality test on Fermi-LAT blazar flux distributions — NOT a comparison against established jet power models. Deviation from normality in blazar flux distributions is well-known and does not constitute evidence for ΔP_間. A proper test requires residual analysis against Blandford-Znajek predictions with beaming and selection bias corrections. This version includes the full author's correction. See CORRECTION_19714365.md for details.

The paper argues that the I-gen corresponds structurally to the domain designated as divine (神仏の領域) across Shinto, Buddhist, Abrahamic, Taoist, and Neoplatonic traditions — not metaphorically, but structurally.
